HIGH H1: row 5 DYNAMIC_CONFIG_STARTUP_CONTROLLER_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS states a spent outcome the code does not produce: dynamic-config-startup-wiring.js withTimeout (76-107) rejects on the timer but never cancels the wrapped promise; on rejection the wiring sets its local controller to null (438-449) while raft-adaptive-timing-controller.js initialize() (220-232) keeps running: loadConfig, registerWatchers (331-349), detectCurrentProfile, initialized = true, startLoop (355-366, setInterval) if enabled, and a later adaptiveTimingEnabled=true starts the loop via the orphan's own watcher (606-613); the wiring's shutdown (492-501) only shuts the controller it holds, so the orphan's interval and watchers are never released; adaptiveTimingEnabled defaults false (config-definitions.js:41). Consequence: a spent bound orphans a controller (R13 unowned lifetime) rather than disabling adaptive timing; repair shape (2) applied literally to row 5 (re-drive initialize later) would create a second controller beside the orphan; the correct shape for row 5 is own or cancel the in-flight initialize (sweep-timer item 1; owner-interaction item 9). Row 4 (INITIAL_READ 300 ms) does hold: the spent read is warned and skipped, applyRaftTimingConfig runs with the configManager value, no re-drive without a later config change (dynamic-config-service get() only fills a cache on late resolve; notifyWatchers only from set/CDC), so the headline load-changes-configuration survives on row 4 alone and the two rows must be separated.
